title: Even on Starless Nights
mood: Torn into the dark behind the world, Vexana falls, and the star at her collar will not go out.

hero.alt: Vexana in her Academy uniform falls head first through the dark, arms open and eyes closed, her long black hair streaming around her.
hero.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana comic, page 19

segs.t: The tower had lost its roof long ago. Vexana stood where its top floor ended in broken stone, high above the dead ground.
Below her ran streets nobody had lived in since the Catastrophe. Doorways with no doors. Weeds in every crack.

Past the last ruins rose the dome. From out here it was only a faint shell of light over Terrinia. Inside it the city glittered. On its cliff stood the Academy’s tower, its white-cyan beam climbing into the night.
She found the girls’ wing without looking for it. One window was lit.
It was the hour when she used to call.
Her phone lay on her desk across the city, where she had left it when the alarm went. She had nothing to call with.
The wind pulled at her cloak. On the day of the corridor she had owned no cloak.
Before dawn the door that had brought her would open behind her, as it always did. Until then, the errand done, the night was hers.
At her right wrist, inside her sleeve, a small gold star was glowing. She laid two fingers over it, through the cloth.
It had been lit since the first hour.
The void. The first hour.
The portal shut on the sight of Guinevere’s hand, still reaching.
Then there was no floor. No wall, no ceiling. No light but the Ender’s.
This was the void, the dark behind the world, where the Enders came from. Chang’e had named it in class. Nobody could get near it.
The claw was still closed on her hand. It dragged her a long way through the dark.
She struck at it with her staff. She twisted against its grip and kicked at nothing. The blades did not loosen.
Then, all at once, it let go.
It was sent to take,
thought Vexana.
Not to kill.
The Ender turned away. The dark carried it off, and its violet glow shrank to a point and went out. It did not look back once.
She slung her staff across her back by its strap. Then she opened her wings of aspirant power. They lit only her white gloves and the toes of her boots. Past them there was nothing at all.
There was no up and no ground. She could not tell if she was falling or floating.
“Guinevere!”
The dark took the word and gave nothing back. She did not call again.
Stay back.
She had shouted it in the corridor without a thought. Now the words came back to her in another voice.
She had heard them last from her father’s back.

That day the shelter by the wall had shaken with every blast. Strangers cried in the dark. He had told her to stay back. She had slipped out to find him anyway, because she was afraid to be alone. An Ender found her first, tall and gray, its claw raised.
Then he was there. He had turned back from his gun and planted himself between them. All she saw was his coat, and his boots set wide on the stones.
“Stay back,” he said. It was the last thing he ever said to her.
A soldier carried her off down the street. Over the man’s shoulder she watched her father’s back. He stayed. Her hands had closed into fists.
This time she was the one who stayed behind.
She saw Guinevere’s hand again, still reaching at the door. Its black glove was whole. No claw had touched it.
It’s all right,
thought Vexana.
She’s safe.
Her fists opened, one finger at a time. Since the shelter she had owed a life. She had carried it through every rule she kept and every dawn in the training yard.
Now it’s paid,
she thought.
Her face was wet. She let it be. The only sound in the dark was her own breathing.
She folded her wings and stopped reaching for anything.
She shut her eyes and let herself fall.
Arms open, her long black hair streaming past her face, she fell for a long time. It was easy.
Then warmth touched her collar.
She opened her eyes. A faint gold point glowed there, the Emblem of Hope. Against her wings it had been too faint to see.
It glowed only when their powers were in sync. Somewhere past all this dark, Guinevere’s star was lit too.
Vexana closed her hand over it. Light burst gold between her fingers and lit her face.

media.alt: Falling upside down, Vexana closes her gloved hand over the gold star at her collar, and light bursts across her wet, wide-open eyes.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana comic, page 21

segs.t: She bent her head to her fist and whispered. “Even on starless nights, the Aspirant emblem guides me.”
Its warmth went into her palm. She held on.
Then the memories came.
Open dark ground at the dome’s edge, long past curfew. Guinevere’s hand tight in hers. Pink and gold bursts cracked open overhead, one after another.
Guinevere pointed up at the sky. Vexana watched her face instead.
“We’ll be just like fireworks, shining at our absolute brightest!” said Guinevere.
A rooftop in the sun, with green guardrails. Guinevere held out a small gold star on her palm. Band-aids wrapped her fingertips, where the solder had burned her.
“Look at this!” said Guinevere. “I made a suuuper amazing invention! With this, we’ll battle side-by-side forever!”
She pinned it at Vexana’s collar. Under Vexana’s fingertip, one seam ran a hair crooked.

The ceremony. Before the photo, Vexana had reached over and straightened Guinevere’s crooked bow. Guinevere had let her. Then they stood hand in hand, badges of honor on their chests. Lesley smiled at them. Behind them the others cheered.
“We’re the best partners in The Aspirants!” said Guinevere.
Vexana grabbed her head with both hands.
Each memory hurt. Guinevere was in every one of them, and Guinevere was not here.
And each one made the star burn brighter.
The light spread over her gloves and up her sleeves, into the ends of her floating hair. Then it reached out into the dark itself, where a moment before there had been nothing.
She did not know how long she fell. Long enough to live the whole year again.
Guinevere,
she thought.
You haven’t let go.
Her hand opened. She reached out into the lit dark, the way Guinevere had reached for her at the door.
Then I won’t either.
Her wings spread again, full of gold. The star blazed at her collar, brighter than it had ever been. Tears ran from her eyes into her hair. She kept looking.
For a while there was only her breathing, and the light around her open hand.

media.alt: Vexana falls through the dark wrapped in rays of light; then, close, the gold star at her collar shines over her face.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana motion comic

segs.t: Then the dark was gone, and the sky was blue.

A shady tree on the Academy lawn. Yellow leaves drifting down. Their badges were still pinned on from the morning. Guinevere’s two drones sat in the grass beside them, round and still, like two gray cats asleep in the sun.
Guinevere lay with her head in Vexana’s lap, her long hair spread over the grass. Vexana’s hand rested on that hair. She had never patted anyone’s hair before today. She was still learning how hard.
“Teacher Chang’e told us,” said Guinevere, to the leaves, “to defeat the Will of the Planet, we must destroy The Enders’ Control Core hidden in its dark void.”
“But we can’t get near the void,” said Vexana.
Guinevere sat bolt upright, eyes squeezed shut, grinning. “Don’t worry!”
Her fist shot out at the sky.
“I will definitely,” she said.
A sound like ice giving. A thin black line ran down the blue behind her.
Guinevere did not open her eyes. “...find a way...”
The line split wider. Something silver pushed through it, many-bladed. Only Vexana saw it.
“...to destroy it!”

media.alt: Comic panel: a black crack splits a blue sky and silver claws push through it, while a bubble says find a way.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana comic, page 34

media.alt: Comic panel: Guinevere sits in the grass, eyes shut and grinning, one fist thrust at the sky, as the claw hangs through the crack over her head.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana comic, page 35

segs.t: At the last word the crack ran down through Guinevere, through her grin and the gold star at her collar.
Above her head the black tore open. The claw hung there in the blue sky of the memory, its blades spread over Guinevere’s head. The leaves went on falling.
